title: Normalise by column and by row, and send the gradient back
brief: Rescale a group to mean 0 and variance 1, build batch norm and layer norm forward, then write their backward passes and check them against finite differences.
hints: normalise_group: subtract x.mean(), then divide by np.sqrt(x.var() + eps). np.var already divides by the number of values, which is what you want.
batchnorm_forward reduces over axis 0 and layernorm_forward over axis 1. Pass keepdims=True to mean and var so the results broadcast against x.
Compute istd = 1 / np.sqrt(var + eps) and xhat = (x - mean) * istd, and return out = gamma * xhat + beta. The cache is the tuple (xhat, istd, gamma, axis).
affine_param_grads sums over axis 0 for both layers: dbeta = dout.sum(axis=0) and dgamma = (dout * xhat).sum(axis=0). gamma and beta have one entry per feature and are shared by every example.

The input gradient is dx = (istd / M) * (M * dxhat - dxhat.sum(axis, keepdims=True) - xhat * (dxhat * xhat).sum(axis, keepdims=True)), with dxhat = dout * gamma and M = dout.shape[axis]. Batch norm and layer norm differ only in the axis stored in the cache, so one helper can serve both backward functions.
Check your dx against a finite difference of the scalar np.sum(dout * forward(x)[0]). If the check fails by a small amount everywhere, look at the sign of the variance term.
